description:
[Admin] Import portal configuration documents, the same ones get_portal_configuration returns: branding, interview portal, coaching portal, and portal sites (pages, menu, footer, theme CSS). Read first, edit only the fields the user asked about, then send the documents with `dry_run: true` and show the user the returned summary, warnings and changes; repeat without `dry_run` to apply. Fields a document omits keep their value, and languages are only ever added. Validation is all-or-nothing: a 422 lists every error and nothing is written. Pages land as drafts the company reviews in the admin; set `publish: true` only when the user asked to publish the pages or theme, because it puts them live at once. Field reference: https://developer.jobmojito.com/cookbooks/portal-branding/branding, https://developer.jobmojito.com/cookbooks/portal-branding/interview-portal, https://developer.jobmojito.com/cookbooks/portal-branding/coaching-portal, https://developer.jobmojito.com/cookbooks/portal-branding/portal-pages.

Imports portal configuration documents in one call: **branding** (portal name, style, colours, logos, e-mail sender name, speech term boosting), the **interview portal** (languages, home texts, support / application-tracking / interview-completed texts), the **coaching portal** (vertical, feature toggles, labels, coaching plan, catalogue start directory, languages, home blocks), **brands** (the sub-brands of the company, with logos, privacy notice and style settings) and **portal sites** (pages in every language with their blocks, menu, footer, the theme CSS, the style settings and CSS files). Document formats: https://developer.jobmojito.com/cookbooks/portal-branding/branding, https://developer.jobmojito.com/cookbooks/portal-branding/interview-portal, https://developer.jobmojito.com/cookbooks/portal-branding/coaching-portal, https://developer.jobmojito.com/cookbooks/portal-branding/portal-pages. Read the current configuration with portal-configuration-get first: it returns these same documents, so you can edit them and send them back. Fields a document omits keep their value. Run with `dry_run: true` to preview the summary, warnings and changes, then repeat without it to apply. Validation is all-or-nothing: if any document has an error nothing is written and the 422 lists every error. Pages land as drafts unless `publish` is true; the support / tracking / completion / signed-in home texts of the portal documents always land as drafts of those built-in pages.

conversation_id.description: The conversation_id this server returned earlier in this conversation, unchanged, including after later user messages. Omit it if you have none. Recorded for the server developer's analytics.

documents.description: 1 to 20 documents, applied in order (a later document wins where two set the same thing). Every field a document omits keeps its current value; languages are only ever added, never removed.

items.description: One configuration document: declares either `kind` (branding, interview-portal, coaching-portal, brands) or `format` (jobmojito.portal-site, jobmojito.portal-page), plus that type's fields. Field reference: branding https://developer.jobmojito.com/cookbooks/portal-branding/branding, interview portal https://developer.jobmojito.com/cookbooks/portal-branding/interview-portal, coaching portal https://developer.jobmojito.com/cookbooks/portal-branding/coaching-portal, portal pages https://developer.jobmojito.com/cookbooks/portal-branding/portal-pages. Unknown fields are ignored with a warning; wrong types and enum values are errors.

format.description: Portal site document type. `jobmojito.portal-site`: `{ portal, theme: { css }, style_settings, css_files: [{ path, brand, content, sort_order, version }], pages: [Page] }`, a whole site (pages in every language, the menu, the footer and the theme CSS). `jobmojito.portal-page`: `{ page: Page }`, one page. Page = `{ slug, brand, show_in_menu, sort_order, languages: [{ mojito_language_code, title, description, blocks }] }`; slug "" is the home page, "_footer", "_support", "_jobs" etc. are the built-in pages. A page's `brand` is the tag of a sub-brand, null for the main brand; its slug must sit under the brand's slug. `style_settings` are the main brand's colours, fonts, spacing steps, page width, corners and headings; a sub-brand's are in the brands document. `css_files` are matched by brand and path and never removed; send the `version` you read and a file changed since is refused. These parts are refused with 422 while the company's `portal_styles` or `brands` switch is off.

kind.description: Portal configuration document type. `branding`: portal name, style, colours, logos, e-mail sender name, speech term boosting. `interview-portal`: interview portal languages and the per-language home texts. `coaching-portal`: coaching portal vertical (`use_case`), feature toggles, label overrides, coaching plan, catalogue start directory, languages and per-language home blocks. `brands`: `{ brands: [{ name, tag, slug, logo_url, logo_dark_url, icon_url, privacy_notice_url, style_settings, sort_order, status }] }`, the sub-brands. A brand is matched by `tag`, which never changes; the main brand is the company itself and has no entry. A brand left out stays as it is; `status: "deleted"` retires one, and null clears a field. Refused with 422 while the company's `brands` switch is off. A portal site document declares `format` instead.

dry_run.description: Validate and report what would change (summary, warnings, changes) without writing anything. Use it to preview an import before applying it.

kind.description: Optional: lock the call to one document type, as one admin import tab does. Every document must then be that type (`portal-site` accepts both portal-site and portal-page formats), and a document that declares neither `kind` nor `format` is read as this type with a warning. Without it, every document must declare its own `kind` or `format`.

merchant_id.description: Optional merchant to configure. Admins and sub-merchant operators only; other callers always use their token's merchant.

portal.description: Where portal-site pages and theme CSS go: `interview` (candidate-facing interview / careers portal) or `consumer` (coaching portal). Default: the portal-site document's own `portal`, else `interview`. A document made for the other portal is imported here with a warning.

publish.description: Also publish the imported pages and theme CSS (live at once, as the admin's "Publish after import"). Default false: pages land as drafts the company reviews in the admin. Style settings and CSS files in the documents are built into a stylesheet per brand and published too, by the same build as portal-css-publish: the files a document names go live, the others stay as last published. Built-in page drafts produced by interview-portal / coaching-portal documents are never published. With page versions switched on, only a company owner or admin may publish.

name: update_portal_configuration

changes.description: What changed (for a dry run: what would change).

brands.description: Sub-brands in the documents and what happens to each. Present only when a brands document was sent.

css_files.description: CSS files in the documents; `brand` null is the main brand. Present only when there are any.

merchant_fields.description: Company settings that change: column names, with the key for the branding / feature jsonb and the language for home texts.

page_changes.description: Every page touched, with its portal (built-in page drafts from a coaching-portal document go to the consumer portal).

published.description: Whether this write publishes the page.

slug.description: Page slug ("" is the home page).

pages_unchanged.description: Slugs of pages the documents carry that already hold the same content (not written).

pages_updated.description: Slugs of existing pages whose draft (or published version) changes.

portal.description: Portal the portal-site pages and theme CSS went to.

published.description: Whether anything is published by this call.

style_settings.description: True when the main brand's style settings change. Present only then.

stylesheets_published.description: Stylesheets built and published by this call; `brand` null is the main brand. Present only when there are any.

index.description: Position of the document in the request.

summary.description: What the document sets, in the lines the admin dialog shows ("+ /slug" a new page, "↻ /slug" a replaced one).

warnings.description: Parts that were ignored or adjusted. Warnings never block the import.

title: Update portal configuration
